consumer.outcome: Where you are: Tessera's parser/logical plan and pull-based executor are done; the active milestone is the rule-based optimizer (the cost-based join ordering comes after, per your 2026-08-04 decision). Your optimizer runs rules bottom-up with transform_up and repeats until nothing changes (capped at 50 passes); rules done: merge adjacent Filters, drop a no-op Project, fold `1 = 1` and drop Filter(true); you snapshot the optimized plan for 20 example queries. Your recorded next action (workspace, 2026-09-09) and your 2026-09-10 todo: filter-below-join (only when the predicate's columns come from one side), projection pruning, the property test execute(optimize(q)) == execute(q), and the open worry that merge-filters vs split-filters could stop the optimizer from terminating. Your weekly log for 2026-09-14 says you didn't touch Tessera that week. Limits: per your 2026-08-24 decision, Tessera plus the dataframe module get at most two evenings a week, and Statistical Learning (exam 2026-10-06) is primary. Coordination also says Tessera must not run ahead of the dataframe query-plan unit, which is at stage 2 with plan 1 of 3 annotated. Plan 1 is exactly filter pushdown and column pruning, so tonight's rule isn't ahead of it. Suggested hour: (1) ~10 min: a result-comparison test for a join+filter query, executing the query before and after optimizing and comparing the rows (a first, fixed-query version of your property test). (2) ~35 min: implement filter-below-join as one transform_up rule, Filter(p, Join(L, R)) → Join(Filter(p, L), R) when every column of p is in L's schema (and the mirror case for R). Push only whole predicates for now and don't add a split-conjunction rule tonight: that is exactly the merge/split fight you worried about. (3) ~15 min: re-run the 20 plan snapshots and read each changed diff before accepting it (your own warning in the snapshot note). Leave projection pruning, its ordering question and termination for the next evening.
